name: Korean Air Cargo (1984 sky blue)
description: Korean Air's 1984 sky-blue scheme on the freighters: pale sky blue above, silver-gray below, no windows; the red-and-blue taegeuk large on the blue fin and on the engines; 'KOREAN AIR CARGO' in big navy capitals over the forward fuselage with the taegeuk as the O of KOREAN, 대한항공 small by the forward door.

logos.description: The 1984 taegeuk: a circle split by an S-curve, red above and blue below, a white 'propeller' stripe running through the S between them, all inside a thin white ring.
The taegeuk small on the outboard cowl.
The taegeuk on the outer face of the blue winglet, low down.
A small Taegukgi at the fin tip.
The SkyTeam Cargo badge (SkyTeam's swirl with 'CARGO' under it), small above the cockpit door.

titles.style: Bold flared serif capitals in navy (the 1984 Korean Air wordmark extended with CARGO), the O of KOREAN replaced by the taegeuk.
Small Hangul under the cockpit on the left side, bold sans.
Small Hangul under the cockpit on the right side too (HL8077, 2025-10-24).

notes: The 1984 scheme with 'KOREAN AIR CARGO': every freighter still wears it in 2024-2026 photos (777Fs HL8045 2026-03, HL8226 2026-06, HL8077 2025-10; 747-8F HL7639 2026-03). No freighter was found in the 2025 livery (standard) by Nov 2026; when one is repainted it will need its own entry. Titles measured on HL8077 (777F, level, right side, nose to the right). The blue/gray split is the passenger file's (the freighters have no windows to set it by; it runs at the same height). Re-checked 2026-11-15: the Hangul title given a length and added on the right side, where HL8077 shows it under the cockpit as on the left (0.037, the 777-300ER's Hangul in metres on the 777F); the cargo title as measured.
history: Korean Air Cargo's freighters have worn the 1984 sky-blue scheme with the CARGO title since the 1980s; the 2025 rebrand has not reached them yet.
